entries.subject: Lunch at the commissary
entries.body: {sender} writes: "Come by the lot this week. Nothing formal — soup, sandwiches, and one or two things better said off the record."

choices.label: Accept the invitation (1⏱)
choices.outcome: Soup, sandwiches, and by coffee a name or two that will matter. Lot lunches are never just lunch.

choices.label: Send polite regrets
choices.outcome: A courteous note goes back. Nobody is offended — and nobody remembers you were asked.

entries.subject: Invitation: Children's Hospital Benefit
entries.body: Gilt edges, heavy paper: {sender} requests the pleasure of your company — and, more importantly, of your checkbook.

choices.label: Send a generous donation (−{money_fmt:150})
choices.outcome: Your name appears on the patrons' list, tastefully high. Generosity, publicly performed, is never wasted in this town.

choices.label: Attend in person (1⏱)
choices.outcome: Two hours of small talk in a good cause. The cause profits — and so does your address book.

choices.label: Quietly toss it
choices.outcome: The envelope lands in the wastebasket. Some absences are noticed; most are not.

entries.subject: A sack of admirers' mail
entries.body: The office forwards a bundle of letters — admirers, hopefuls, one marriage proposal, two scripts, and a drawing of you that is either flattering or libelous.

choices.label: Answer a few personally
choices.outcome: A dozen replies in your own hand. Somewhere out there, a dozen people will never say a bad word about you.

choices.label: Let the assistant handle it
choices.outcome: Form letters with a decent signature stamp. Efficient, invisible, forgotten by Friday.

choices.label: Into the drawer with it
choices.outcome: The drawer swallows another bundle. One day that drawer will be an archive — or a fire hazard.

entries.subject: Inquiry from the revenue office
entries.body: Dry language, official stamp: certain private expenditures have "attracted attention." You are invited to clarify.

choices.label: Pay the accountant to make it airtight (−{money_fmt:80})
choices.outcome: Three folders, one afternoon, zero findings. Expensive, boring, correct — exactly how you want your taxes.

choices.label: Ignore it — they're fishing
choices.outcome: Weeks pass. Nothing. Sometimes the bureaucracy simply loses interest.
choices.outcome_fail: The second letter is registered mail. The third has numbers in it. You pay — with penalty, and with a small paragraph in the trade press.

entries.subject: Request for comment
entries.body: {sender} needs a quote for tomorrow's column — about the town, the business, and "where it is all heading." Deadline: tonight.

choices.label: Give them a good line
choices.outcome: Your sentence sits in print, sharp and quotable. The town reads it over breakfast — with your name attached.
choices.outcome_fail: The quote reads differently in print than it sounded on the phone. Lesson: there is no such thing as harmless.

choices.label: "No comment."
choices.outcome: Two words, correctly deployed, are also a statement. The column runs without you — this time.

entries.subject: An unsolicited screenplay
entries.body: Brown paper, typewritten label, no agency stamp: a script from nowhere. The first page is — surprisingly — not terrible.

choices.label: Read it over the weekend (1⏱)
choices.outcome: Most of it is apprentice work — but two scenes have teeth, and reading raw pages keeps your eye sharp.

choices.label: Return to sender
choices.outcome: Back in the mail with a printed courtesy slip. The town is full of first pages.

entries.subject: "You probably don't remember me…"
entries.body: A name from years ago — someone from before the agency, before the title, before all of it. They are in town for a week and would like to see you.

choices.label: Make time for them (1⏱)
choices.outcome: Two hours with someone who knew you before you mattered. Cheaper than any doctor, and twice as honest — a friendship outside the business.

choices.label: Have the office send regrets
choices.outcome: A polite note on agency paper. Some doors close so quietly you never hear it.

entries.subject: A career takes its next step
entries.body: Word arrives with the morning mail: {sender} has moved up in the world. The town resorts itself around news like this — and remembers who wrote first.

choices.label: Send warm congratulations

effects.text: You were among the first to congratulate.

choices.outcome: Your note is on their new desk before the nameplate is. First congratulations are remembered longest.

choices.label: Congratulate — and remind them, gently, of old times

effects.text: Congratulated — with a soft reminder of who was kind early.

choices.outcome: Warmth with a fine thread of memory woven in. They smile — and they understand.

choices.label: Let it pass
choices.outcome: No note, no call. Risen people keep score more carefully than struggling ones.

entries.subject: A request for a face-to-face
entries.body: {sender} writes briefly, almost curtly: there is something that should not be discussed on paper. Could you make time this week?

choices.label: Take the meeting
choices.outcome: You clear an afternoon.

choices.label: Send regrets
choices.outcome: A polite refusal. Whatever it was, someone else will hear it first now.

entries.subject: An old debt, courteously recalled
entries.body: {sender} writes — friendly, and only once: "You will remember that I helped you when it mattered. It would mean something to me if that were not forgotten."

choices.label: Repay in kind (uses one of your favors)
choices.outcome: One call, one favor redirected, one ledger balanced. This is how the town keeps its books.

choices.label: Settle it generously (−{money_fmt:120})
choices.outcome: Money is the bluntest way to pay a social debt — but paid is paid, and generosity is remembered.

choices.label: Let them wait
choices.outcome: No reply. In this town, unpaid debts do not disappear — they compound, in whispers.

entries.subject: A note that is not about business
entries.body: A short letter from {sender} — no agency matter, no favor, no angle. Just an invitation to dinner, for its own sake. When did you last get one of those?

choices.label: Say yes (1⏱)
choices.outcome: Dinner runs long, and for once nobody at the table wants anything from you. You will see each other again.

choices.label: Decline — the work comes first
choices.outcome: You write a courteous no. The work is still there in the morning. It always is.

entries.subject: An evening that belongs to you two
entries.body: {sender} suggests an evening — no premiere, no table full of producers. Just the two of you, somewhere quiet.

choices.label: Keep the evening free (1⏱)
choices.outcome: For a few hours the town does not exist. You come back lighter — and remembered why.

choices.label: Cancel — the week is on fire
choices.outcome: You cancel, kindly, with reasons. Reasons are what one always has.

entries.subject: "We need to talk."
entries.body: {sender} is not angry, which is worse. The premieres you missed, the calls at dinner, the town that always comes first — it has a price, and it is being named now.

choices.label: Talk it out — honestly (1⏱)
choices.outcome: A long evening, some of it hard to hear. But the air is clear afterward — clearer than in months.

choices.label: Bury it under a gift
choices.outcome: The bracelet is beautiful. The silence it buys is not.

entries.subject: A question, long overdue
entries.body: Between two ordinary sentences, {sender} asks the question that changes the shape of a life. The town, for once, has no opinion you care about.

choices.label: Yes.
choices.outcome: Yes. The rest of the week is paperwork and champagne, in that order.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.outcome: "Not yet" is an answer that ages badly. You both pretend it didn't.

entries.subject: You are expected
entries.body: {sender} writes, in a hand that assumes acceptance: "Saturday. Everyone will be there. Do not disappoint me."

choices.label: Accept — of course
choices.outcome: The invitation goes into your breast pocket. Attend it from the Contacts desk when the evening comes.

choices.label: Decline
choices.outcome: One does not decline {sender} twice. You may have just used your once.
